nodes.description: A single allele accounts for the whole disease: c.35A>G, replacing the highly conserved tyrosine at position 12 of the epsilon subunit with cysteine, homozygous in all three reported patients and absent from controls. Epsilon is the smallest F1 subunit and the only one with no bacterial or chloroplast homologue, sitting in the central stalk with gamma and delta. The mutant protein is made and is incorporated into the enzyme — this is not a null allele — but its presence depresses the biosynthesis of the complex.

nodes.description: The primary biochemical lesion is a shortage of assembled enzyme, not a broken enzyme. Mitochondrial content of the ATP synthase complex falls by 60-70 percent in patient fibroblasts, matching the fall in activity; the complex that is present is of normal size and contains the mutant epsilon subunit, and it hydrolyses and synthesises normally. F1 and Fo subunits fall together, and the reduction of the assembled 600 kDa complex is not accompanied by F1 subcomplexes — the enzyme fails to be built rather than falling apart after assembly. Silencing ATP5F1E in HEK293 cells reproduces this without any patient allele, confirming that reduced epsilon dosage alone is sufficient.

nodes.description:
This node exists to state the boundary of the entity. The ATP5F1E lesion is an ISOLATED complex V deficiency: the electron-transport complexes are not reduced, and in the index patient's fibroblasts they were increased, an apparently compensatory change that does not rescue the energetic defect. That is what separates MC5DN3 from the combined-OXPHOS presentations in which complex V deficiency is one component among several, and it is the biochemical signature that points a diagnostic workup at the nuclear ATP-synthase genes.
Conformance note: the module node pairs decreased oxidative phosphorylation with increased reactive oxygen species. Only the first half is evidenced here. A ROS increase is a reasonable inference from the raised state-3 membrane potential, and the same review that reports that potential makes the electron-leak argument - but it demonstrates the ROS rise in TMEM70-lacking fibroblasts, not in ATP5F1E ones, so the ROS arm is not asserted. The module's upstream node, age-related mitochondrial damage and mtDNA mutation, does not apply to a primary nuclear-gene subunit defect, so conformance is declared at this node alone.

nodes.description: The one asymmetry in the biochemistry, and the reason this lesion says something about enzyme biogenesis. Every investigated F1 and Fo subunit falls in proportion to the assembled complex except subunit c, which instead accumulates in a detergent-insoluble form. The same accumulation appears in ATP5F1E-silenced HEK293 cells, where subunit c is found in 200-400 kDa subcomplexes containing neither F1 nor other Fo subunits. This implicates the epsilon subunit in loading the hydrophobic c-ring onto the rotor, a role distinct from stabilising F1.
